Base directory for this skill: D:\code\invesments\master_investments_mmo\.claude\skills\cook # Cook - Smart Feature Implementation End-to-end implementation with automatic workflow detection. **Principles:** YAGNI, KISS, DRY | Token efficiency | Concise reports ## Usage ``` /ck:cook ``` **IMPORTANT:** If no flag is provided, the skill will use the `interactive` mode by default for the workflow. **Optional flags to select the workflow mode:** - `--interactive`: Full workflow with user input (**default**) - `--fast`: Skip research, scout→plan→code - `--parallel`: Multi-agent execution - `--no-test`: Skip testing step - `--auto`: Auto-approve all steps **Composable flags** (combine with any mode): - `--tdd`: Tests-first per phase — write tests for current behavior before refactoring, then verify they still pass after the implementation step **Example:** ``` /ck:cook "Add user authentication to the app" --fast /ck:cook path/to/plan.md --auto /ck:cook "Refactor auth middleware" --tdd ``` Do NOT write implementation code until a plan exists and has been reviewed. This applies regardless of task simplicity. "Simple" tasks are where unexamined assumptions waste the most time. Exception: `--fast` mode skips research but still requires a plan step. User override: If user explicitly says "just code it" or "skip planning", respect their instruction. Before planning OR asking clarifying questions, scan the codebase. Mandatory scout outputs: 1. Project type, language(s), framework(s) 2. Existing modules/files relevant to the task 3. Current patterns/conventions for similar features (so the implementation matches them) 4. Existing docs in `./docs/` and any in-flight plans in `./plans/` covering this area 5. Public APIs, schemas, contracts that the task could affect State a 3-6 bullet codebase-context summary to the user before asking questions. Skip ONLY when input is a `plan.md`/`phase-*.md` path (the plan already encodes scout output). Before producing a plan, you MUST be able to answer ALL of these in one concrete sentence each (use `AskUserQuestion` to pin them down — do NOT proceed on vague intent): 1. **Expected output**: the concrete artifact(s) the user will see at the end (file paths, feature behavior, UI screen, API endpoint + payload, CLI command + flags). 2. **Acceptance criteria**: specific behaviors / inputs → outputs / edge cases that MUST work to call it "done". 3. **Scope boundary**: what is explicitly OUT of scope this round. 4. **Non-negotiable constraints**: stack, file locations, naming, backward compatibility, deadlines, performance. 5. **Touchpoints**: which existing files/modules (from scout) will be modified or extended; which contracts must stay stable. Ground every `AskUserQuestion` option in scout findings (e.g., "Add to `src/api/users.ts` (matches existing pattern) or new `src/api/profile.ts`?"). Skip ONLY when input is a `plan.md`/`phase-*.md` path. Implementation is NOT done until verified to be side-effect-free. Code-review and test gates MUST prove: 1. New behavior matches every acceptance criterion above. 2. All tests pass — including tests in modules that share files/contracts with the change. 3. No existing business logic / workflow regression: explicitly walk each touchpoint and any caller of changed functions. 4. No new lint/type/build errors anywhere in the repo. 5. Public contracts unchanged unless intentional and called out (function signatures, exported types, API responses, DB schemas, env vars, config keys). User override: If user invoked `--no-test`, item 2 is downgraded to a warning. Surface the unverified-tests risk in the finalize `AskUserQuestion` so the user accepts the trade-off rather than having it silently chosen. Items 1, 3, 4, 5 remain enforceable via the mandatory `code-reviewer` subagent. If review/testing reveals a side effect, regression, or broken workflow, STOP. Use `AskUserQuestion` to present: - What broke (file, test, workflow, user-facing behavior) - Why this implementation caused it (1-line cause) - 2-4 concrete options for the user to choose, e.g.: - "Revert this slice and re-plan with stricter scope" - "Keep the implementation and update to match the new contract" - "Add a compatibility shim at so old callers keep working" - "Accept the regression — old behavior was unintended/buggy" Let the user decide. Do not silently patch around regressions. ## Anti-Rationalization | Thought | Reality | |---------|---------| | "This is too simple to plan" | Simple tasks have hidden complexity. Plan takes 30 seconds. | | "I already know how to do this" | Knowing ≠ planning. Write it down. | | "Let me just start coding" | Undisciplined action wastes tokens. Plan first. | | "The user wants speed" | Fastest path = plan → implement → done. Not: implement → debug → rewrite. | | "I'll plan as I go" | That's not planning, that's hoping. | | "Just this once" | Every skip is "just this once." No exceptions. | ## Smart Intent Detection | Input Pattern | Detected Mode | Behavior | |---------------|---------------|----------| | Path to `plan.md` or `phase-*.md` | code | Execute existing plan | | Contains "fast", "quick" | fast | Skip research, scout→plan→code | | Contains "trust me", "auto" | auto | Auto-approve all steps | | Lists 3+ features OR "parallel" | parallel | Multi-agent execution | | Contains "no test", "skip test" | no-test | Skip testing step | | Default | interactive | Full workflow with user input | See `references/intent-detection.md` for detection logic. ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Intent Detection] --> B{Has plan path?} B -->|Yes| F[Load Plan] B -->|No| C{Mode?} C -->|fast| D[Scout → Plan → Code] C -->|interactive/auto| SC[Scout Codebase MANDATORY] SC --> SR[Summarize Findings to User] SR --> RQ{Exact requirements captured?
output, acceptance, scope, constraints, touchpoints} RQ -->|No| SR RQ -->|Yes| E[Research → Review → Plan] E --> F D --> F F --> G[Review Gate] G -->|approved| H[Implement] G -->|rejected| E H --> H1{Simplify signal?} H1 -->|Yes| H2[Conditional Simplify] H1 -->|No| I[Review Gate] H2 --> I I -->|approved| J{--no-test?} J -->|No| K[Test] J -->|Yes| L[Finalize] K --> L L --> M[Report + Journal] ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** Prose sections below provide detail for each node. If prose conflicts with this flow, follow the diagram. ## Workflow Overview ``` [Intent Detection] → [Research?] → [Review] → [Plan] → [Review] → [Implement] → [Conditional Simplify?] → [Review] → [Test?] → [Review] → [Finalize] ``` **Default (non-auto):** Stops at `[Review]` gates for human approval before each major step. **Auto mode (`--auto`):** Skips human review gates, implements all phases continuously. **Claude Tasks:** Utilize `TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskList` during implementation step. **Fallback:** These are CLI-only tools — unavailable in VSCode extension. If they error, use `TodoWrite` for progress tracking instead. | Mode | Research | Testing | Review Gates | Phase Progression | |------|----------|---------|--------------|-------------------| | interactive | ✓ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | auto | ✓ | ✓ | Auto if score≥9.5 | All at once (no stops) | | fast | ✗ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | parallel | Optional | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | Parallel groups | | no-test | ✓ | ✗ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | code | ✗ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | Per plan | ## Step Output Format ``` ✓ Step [N]: [Brief status] - [Key metrics] ``` ## Blocking Gates (Non-Auto Mode) Human review required at these checkpoints (skipped with `--auto`): - **Post-Research:** Review findings before planning - **Post-Plan:** Approve plan before implementation - **Post-Implementation:** Approve code before testing - **Post-Testing:** 100% pass + approve before finalize **Always enforced (all modes):** - **Testing:** 100% pass required (unless no-test mode) - **Code Review (MANDATORY):** Spawn `code-reviewer` subagent with explicit checks: (a) every acceptance criterion met, (b) no regression to business logic in touchpoints/blast-radius, (c) no breaking changes to public contracts (signatures, schemas, APIs, env vars) unless called out, (d) follows existing patterns from scout, (e) no new lint/type/build errors anywhere. Ask user if they want to commit via `git-manager` subagent 5. Run `/ck:journal` to write a concise technical journal entry upon completion ## Required Subagents (MANDATORY) | Phase | Subagent | Requirement | |-------|----------|-------------| | Research | `researcher` | Optional in fast/code | | Scout | `ck:scout` | Optional in code | | Plan | `planner` | Optional in code | | UI Work | `ui-ux-designer` | If frontend work | | Testing | `tester`, `debugger` | **MUST** spawn | | Review | `code-reviewer` | **MUST** spawn | | Finalize | `/ck:project-management` skill + `docs-manager`, `git-manager` subagents | **MUST** invoke all | **CRITICAL ENFORCEMENT:** - Steps 4, 5, 6 **MUST** use Task tool to spawn subagents - DO NOT implement testing, review, or finalization yourself - DELEGATE - If workflow ends with 0 Task tool calls, it is INCOMPLETE - Pattern: `Task(subagent_type="[type]", prompt="[task]", description="[brief]")` ## References - `references/intent-detection.md` - Detection rules and routing logic - `references/workflow-steps.md` - Detailed step definitions for all modes - `references/review-cycle.md` - Interactive and auto review processes - `references/subagent-patterns.md` - Subagent invocation patterns ## Workflow Position **Typically follows:** `/ck:plan` (execute a plan), `/ck:brainstorm` (implement agreed solution) **Typically precedes:** `/ck:code-review` (review after implementation), `/ck:test` (validate changes) **Related:** `/ck:fix` (alternative for bug fixes), `/ck:plan` (create plan before cooking) ARGUMENTS: plans/260516-2200-operator-evolution-revenue-fitness into master_investments

# Operator Evolution: Revenue-Grounded Fitness Rewiring

## Problem Statement

System has 4-layer self-evolution (template→strategy→meta→meta-meta) technically superior to academic papers (EvoAgentX, AgentEvolver, AEVO). But fitness function is 100% analysis-quality proxies:
- `brier × 0.6 + fact_yield × 0.25 + parse_success × 0.15`

Result: system evolves to be a better ANALYST, not a better MONEY-MAKER. Deal pipeline exists (7 stages) but has 0 entries. No revenue signal feeds evolution.

## Solution

Wire revenue outcomes into fitness function. Extend evolution scope to execution (not just analysis). Add complexity penalty + velocity metric.

**New fitness:** `brier×0.3 + revenue_signal×0.4 + velocity×0.2 + yield×0.1`

## Target Repo

`D:/code/invesments/master_investments` (all code changes there, plan lives in _mmo)

| Phase | Name | Status | Effort |
|-------|------|--------|--------|

| 2 | [Revenue-Grounded Fitness Function](./phase-02-revenue-grounded-fitness-function.md) | Pending | 2d |
| 3 | [Execution Template Evolution](./phase-03-execution-template-evolution.md) | Pending | 3d |
| 4 | [Complexity Penalty and Velocity Metric](./phase-04-complexity-penalty-and-velocity-metric.md) | Pending | 1d |
| 5 | [Integration Test and Cold-Start Bootstrap](./phase-05-integration-test-and-cold-start-bootstrap.md) | Pending | 1d |

## Dependencies

- Depends on completed: `260516-2035-meta-evolution-layer-strategy-level` (L4 strategy evolution infra)

## Key Architectural Insight

Academic self-evolving agent papers (EvoAgentX, AgentEvolver, AlphaEvolve) beat baselines because their fitness = TASK COMPLETION (binary pass/fail). Our system currently lacks this — we measure prediction accuracy (a proxy) not execution success (the terminal metric). This plan fixes that gap.

# Phase 1: Wire Deal Pipeline to Outcome Tracker

## Overview

Create data flow: deal-pipeline stage transitions emit events that outcome_tracker consumes. This enables downstream phases to compute revenue-based fitness. Currently deal pipeline has 7 stages (identified→verified→introduced→facilitating→negotiating→closed→paid) but 0 entries and no connection to evolution system.

## Requirements

- Functional: When a deal moves stages, outcome_tracker records the transition with timestamp + $ amount (if available)
- Functional: When deal reaches "paid" stage, emit `revenue_resolved` event with final amount
- Non-functional: Append-only, no data loss on crash, JSON-line format

## Architecture

```
deal-pipeline.json (stage change)
       ↓
deal-stage-emitter.py (new — detects transitions)
       ↓
outcome_tracker/tracker.py (extended — accepts revenue events)
       ↓
data/calibration/revenue-outcomes.jsonl (new — append-only)
       ↓
evolution/fitness_scorer.py (Phase 2 consumes this)
```

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `.claude/lib/intelligence/outcome_tracker/schemas.py` — add RevenueEvent schema
- Modify: `.claude/lib/intelligence/outcome_tracker/tracker.py` — add `log_revenue_event()` method
- Modify: `.claude/skills/business/feedback_loop/deal-outcome-to-prediction.py` — enhance to emit revenue signal
- Create: `data/calibration/revenue-outcomes.jsonl` — new append-only store
- Read: `data/deals/deal-pipeline.json` — existing pipeline structure
- Read: `.claude/skills/business/deal-tracker/templates/deal-schema.json` — existing schema

## Implementation Steps

1. Add `RevenueEvent` dataclass to `outcome_tracker/schemas.py`:
   ```python
   @dataclass
   class RevenueEvent:
       case_id: str
       stage_from: str
       stage_to: str
       revenue_amount: Optional[float]  # None until "paid" stage
       timestamp: str
       days_since_verdict: int
       linked_verdict_id: Optional[str]
   ```

2. Add `log_revenue_event()` to `outcome_tracker/tracker.py`:
   - Appends to `data/calibration/revenue-outcomes.jsonl`
   - Links to original stage0 verdict via case_id pattern matching

3. Enhance `deal-outcome-to-prediction.py`:
   - Currently bridges deal outcomes to prediction system
   - Add: detect stage transitions by comparing pipeline state to cached previous state
   - Add: compute `days_since_verdict` from linked stage0 case timestamp
   - Add: emit `RevenueEvent` on every stage transition (not just final)

4. Add intermediate reward signals:
   - `identified → verified`: signal = 0.1 (confirmed real opportunity)
   - `verified → introduced`: signal = 0.2 (action taken)
   - `introduced → facilitating`: signal = 0.3 (relationship engaged)
   - `negotiating → closed`: signal = 0.7 (deal committed)
   - `closed → paid`: signal = 1.0 ($ received)

5. Create `data/calibration/revenue-outcomes.jsonl` (empty init file)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] RevenueEvent schema defined with all fields
- [ ] `log_revenue_event()` appends to revenue-outcomes.jsonl
- [ ] deal-outcome-to-prediction.py detects stage transitions
- [ ] Intermediate reward values (0.1→1.0) emitted per stage
- [ ] days_since_verdict computed correctly from linked verdict timestamp
- [ ] Unit test: mock pipeline with 2 deals, verify 3+ events emitted correctly

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|-----------|
| No deals in pipeline yet | Can't test with real data | Create 2 synthetic test deals for validation |
| case_id matching between deal and verdict may be fuzzy | Wrong linking | Use explicit `linked_verdict_id` field, require manual link at deal creation |

52	   def _load_revenue_for_case(self, case_id: str) -> Optional[float]:
53	       """Load cumulative revenue signal (0.0-1.0) for a case from revenue-outcomes.jsonl."""
54	       # Sum intermediate rewards for all stage transitions linked to this case
55	       # Max 1.0 (reached "paid" stage)
56	   ```
57	
58	2. Add velocity scorer:
59	   ```python
60	   def _compute_velocity(self, case_id: str) -> Optional[float]:
61	       """Score based on days_since_verdict for first revenue event."""
62	       # velocity = 1.0 / max(days / 90.0, 0.1)
63	       # 90 days = baseline (score 1.0), faster = bonus, slower = penalty
64	   ```

70	   REVENUE_WEIGHT = 0.4    # NEW
71	   VELOCITY_WEIGHT = 0.2   # NEW
72	   YIELD_WEIGHT = 0.1      # was 0.25
73	   # PARSE_WEIGHT removed (subsumed into yield)
74	
75	   def compute_fitness(self, variant_id: int) -> Optional[float]:
76	       # ... existing Brier + yield logic ...
77	       revenue = self._load_revenue_for_case(case_id)
78	       velocity = self._compute_velocity(case_id)
79	
80	       if revenue is not None:
81	           # Full formula
82	           return (brier_component * 0.3 + revenue * 0.4 +
83	                   velocity * 0.2 + yield_component * 0.1)
84	       else:
85	           # Fallback (no revenue data yet)
86	           return (brier_component * 0.5 + yield_component * 0.3 +
87	                   parse_component * 0.2)
88	   ```

91	   - Strategy fitness = avg fitness of its last N verdicts
92	   - Revenue-producing strategies rank higher
93	
94	5. Update `orchestrator.py` `post_think_hook()` to pass case linkage data through
95	
96	6. Add fallback mode detection:

# Phase 4: Complexity Penalty and Velocity Metric

## Overview

Add two anti-bloat mechanisms: (1) complexity penalty that deducts fitness for overly complex strategies, (2) velocity metric that rewards faster time-to-revenue. Together they create evolutionary pressure toward SIMPLER + FASTER strategies.

## Requirements

- Functional: Strategies with more agents/longer templates score lower (all else equal)
- Functional: Strategies that lead to faster revenue score higher
- Functional: Floor protection — never penalize a strategy with positive revenue attribution
- Non-functional: Max 10% fitness impact from complexity penalty (not dominant)

## Architecture

```
Strategy (agents, templates, gates)
           ↓
┌──────────────────────────────┐
│  Complexity Scorer           │
│  agent_count_penalty         │
│  template_length_penalty     │
│  gate_count_penalty          │
│  → combined complexity tax   │
└──────────────────────────────┘
           ↓
┌──────────────────────────────┐
│  Velocity Scorer             │
│  days_to_first_stage_move    │
│  days_to_revenue             │
│  → velocity_bonus            │
└──────────────────────────────┘
           ↓
fitness_scorer: deduct complexity_tax, add velocity_bonus
```

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `.claude/lib/intelligence/evolution/fitness_scorer.py` — add complexity_penalty term
- Modify: `.claude/lib/intelligence/mechanism/strategy_evolution/fitness.py` — add strategy-level complexity scoring
- Modify: `.claude/lib/intelligence/mechanism/meta_meta.py` — add "complexity_growth" as stagnation signal #5

## Implementation Steps

1. Add complexity scorer to `fitness_scorer.py`:
   ```python
   COMPLEXITY_PENALTY_WEIGHT = 0.1  # max 10% impact

   def _complexity_penalty(self, strategy: dict) -> float:
       """Lower = simpler = better. Returns 0.0-1.0."""
       agent_count = len(strategy.get("wave1_agents", [])) + len(strategy.get("wave2_agents", []))
       agent_penalty = min(agent_count / 20.0, 1.0)  # 20+ agents = max penalty

       template_chars = sum(len(t) for t in strategy.get("templates", {}).values())
       length_penalty = min(template_chars / 10000.0, 1.0)  # 10K+ chars = max

       return (agent_penalty * 0.6 + length_penalty * 0.4)
   ```

2. Add floor protection:
   ```python
   def compute_fitness(self, variant_id: int) -> float:
       base_fitness = ...  # existing + revenue terms
       complexity = self._complexity_penalty(strategy)

       # Floor: if this strategy has positive revenue attribution, skip penalty
       if self._has_positive_revenue(variant_id):
           return base_fitness

       return base_fitness - (complexity * COMPLEXITY_PENALTY_WEIGHT)
   ```

3. Add velocity bonus (already partially in Phase 2, formalize here):
   ```python
   def _velocity_bonus(self, case_id: str) -> float:
       """Bonus for faster strategies. 0.0 = no data, up to 0.2 bonus."""
       days = self._days_to_first_action(case_id)
       if days is None:
           return 0.0
       # 7 days = max bonus, 90 days = zero bonus, >90 = penalty
       if days <= 7:
           return 0.2
       elif days <= 90:
           return 0.2 * (1.0 - (days - 7) / 83.0)
       else:
           return -0.05  # slight penalty for very slow
   ```

4. Add "complexity_growth" stagnation signal to `meta_meta.py`:
   ```python
   def _check_complexity_growth(self, population: list[Strategy]) -> Optional[StagnationSignal]:
       """Detect if population is growing more complex without fitness gain."""
       recent = population[-5:]  # last 5 strategies
       older = population[-10:-5]
       if not older:
           return None
       avg_recent_agents = mean(s.total_agents for s in recent)
       avg_older_agents = mean(s.total_agents for s in older)
       if avg_recent_agents > avg_older_agents * 1.3:  # 30% growth
           return StagnationSignal(
               signal_type="complexity_growth",
               severity=0.6,
               detail=f"Agent count grew {avg_older_agents:.1f}→{avg_recent_agents:.1f} without fitness gain"
           )
       return None
   ```

5. Wire into strategy_evolution `fitness.py`:
   - Deduct complexity penalty from strategy fitness score
   - Log complexity metrics per evaluation for dashboard

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Complexity penalty computed for all strategies (agent_count + template_length)
- [ ] Floor protection: revenue-positive strategies immune to penalty
- [ ] Velocity bonus: 7-day execution scores max bonus
- [ ] meta_meta.py detects complexity_growth stagnation (signal type #5)
- [ ] Unit test: two strategies with same Brier — simpler one scores higher
- [ ] Unit test: revenue-positive strategy NOT penalized despite complexity

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|-----------|
| Penalty kills genuinely useful complex strategies | Lost capability | Floor protection + 10% cap ensures penalty never dominates |
| Velocity bonus rewards premature action | Rushing into bad deals | Velocity only measures time-to-STAGE-MOVE, not time-to-verdict — analysis depth unaffected |

# Phase 5: Integration Test and Cold-Start Bootstrap

## Overview

Bootstrap the system with labeled historical data so evolution can start immediately without waiting months for real deals. Create integration tests proving full loop: verdict → deal → stage transitions → revenue event → fitness update → evolution decision.

## Requirements

- Functional: 5 historical verdicts labeled with hypothetical revenue outcomes
- Functional: End-to-end test proves full data flow works
- Functional: System transitions from "fallback mode" to "revenue mode" after bootstrap
- Non-functional: Bootstrap data clearly marked as synthetic (not confused with real outcomes)

## Architecture

```
Bootstrap Data (5 labeled cases)
         ↓
deal-pipeline.json (seeded with 5 synthetic deals)
         ↓
Full pipeline: emit events → tracker → fitness → evolution
         ↓
Verify: fallback mode → revenue mode transition
```

## Related Code Files

- Create: `data/calibration/bootstrap-revenue-cases.json` — 5 labeled synthetic cases
- Modify: `data/deals/deal-pipeline.json` — seed with bootstrap deals (marked synthetic)
- Create: `.claude/lib/intelligence/evolution/tests/test_revenue_fitness_integration.py`
- Read: All Phase 1-4 modified files for integration verification

## Implementation Steps

1. Label 5 historical verdicts with hypothetical revenue outcomes:
   ```json
   [
     {"case_id": "stage0-260412-compounding-money-model", "observed": 1,
      "hypothetical_revenue": 500, "hypothetical_days": 45,
      "stages_reached": ["identified","verified","introduced"],
      "label_source": "bootstrap_synthetic"},
     {"case_id": "stage0-260412-info-source-audit", "observed": 0,
      "hypothetical_revenue": 0, "hypothetical_days": null,
      "stages_reached": ["identified"],
      "label_source": "bootstrap_synthetic"},
     // ... 3 more cases
   ]
   ```

2. Create bootstrap script that:
   - Reads bootstrap-revenue-cases.json
   - Creates synthetic deal entries in deal-pipeline.json (tagged `"source": "bootstrap"`)
   - Emits RevenueEvents for each stage reached
   - Verifies fitness_scorer transitions from fallback to revenue mode

3. Write integration test `test_revenue_fitness_integration.py`:
   ```python
   def test_full_loop():
       """Verdict → deal → stage → event → fitness → evolution."""
       # Setup: create case with Brier=0.2 (good prediction)
       # Act: emit revenue events (identified → verified → introduced)
       # Assert: fitness score includes revenue_signal term
       # Assert: fitness > fallback-only fitness for same Brier

   def test_velocity_rewards_fast_execution():
       """Faster deals score higher velocity."""
       # Two cases: same revenue, different days_since_verdict
       # Assert: 14-day case scores higher than 60-day case

   def test_complexity_penalty_with_floor():
       """Complex strategy with revenue = no penalty."""
       # Strategy with 15 agents + positive revenue
       # Assert: complexity_penalty NOT applied

   def test_fallback_mode_without_revenue_data():
       """System uses old weights when <3 revenue events."""
       # Assert: fitness uses 0.5/0.3/0.2 weights (fallback)

   def test_transition_to_revenue_mode():
       """After 3+ revenue events, switches to new weights."""
       # Emit 3 events
       # Assert: fitness uses 0.3/0.4/0.2/0.1 weights (revenue mode)
   ```

4. Verify execution template seeding:
   - Confirm 3+ outreach templates loaded in registry
   - Confirm variant_index=0 baselines exist
   - Confirm ExecutionMutator can generate at least 1 variant

5. Dashboard verification:
   - Check evolution-auto-runner.cjs correctly triggers with new components
   - Verify no errors in hook logs after bootstrap

6. Document transition:
   - Update `data/evolution/meta-meta-config.json` to include new stagnation signal
   - Log "SYSTEM: Revenue-grounded fitness ACTIVE" after successful bootstrap

## Success Criteria

- [ ] 5 bootstrap cases labeled and loaded
- [ ] deal-pipeline.json has 5 synthetic entries (tagged "bootstrap")
- [ ] Integration test passes: full loop verdict→fitness works
- [ ] Fallback→revenue mode transition verified
- [ ] Velocity test: fast case scores higher
- [ ] Complexity floor test: revenue-positive immune
- [ ] Execution template seeds loaded (3+ outreach)
- [ ] evolution-auto-runner.cjs runs without errors post-bootstrap
- [ ] System logs "Revenue-grounded fitness ACTIVE"

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|-----------|
| Synthetic data contaminates real evolution | Wrong fitness signal | All bootstrap entries tagged "source": "bootstrap"; excluded after 5 real entries |
| Bootstrap cases don't represent real deal dynamics | Biased initial evolution | Conservative labels (mostly stage 1-2, avoid overconfident revenue claims) |
| Integration test fragile across platforms | CI/CD breaks | Use relative paths, mock time, no network calls |

1	"""
2	Outcome Tracker - Log predictions and decisions to SQLite via db/timeseries.py.
3	
4	Designed to extend the existing /log-outcome skill with intelligence-layer
5	tracking (market predictions, opportunity bets, operator decisions).
6	
7	Storage contract
8	----------------
9	Depends on `.claude/lib/intelligence/db/timeseries.py` (Phase 0A).
10	If that module is not yet available, falls back to local JSON files so this
11	module is independently usable during parallel development.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import json
17	import logging
18	from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
19	from pathlib import Path
20	from typing import Optional
21	from uuid import uuid4
22	
23	from .schemas import Decision, OutcomeCode, Prediction
24	
25	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
26	
27	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
28	# Storage backend abstraction (thin wrapper — swapped when timeseries is ready)
29	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
30	
31	_DB_AVAILABLE = False
32	
33	try:
34	    # Phase 0A delivers this module; import lazily so we don't hard-block
35	    from ..db.timeseries import TimeseriesDB  # type: ignore[import]
36	    _DB_AVAILABLE = True
37	except ImportError:
38	    TimeseriesDB = None  # type: ignore[assignment,misc]
39	
40	
41	class _JsonFallbackStore:
42	    """
43	    Minimal append-only JSON store used when timeseries.py is unavailable.
44	    Two files: predictions.json + decisions.json under data_dir.
45	    """
46	
47	    def __init__(self, data_dir: Path) -> None:
48	        data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
49	        self._predictions_file = data_dir / "predictions.json"
50	        self._decisions_file = data_dir / "decisions.json"
51	
52	    def _load(self, path: Path) -> list[dict]:
53	        if not path.exists():
54	            return []
55	        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
56	            try:
57	                return json.load(fh)
58	            except json.JSONDecodeError:
59	                logger.warning("Corrupt JSON at %s — starting fresh", path)
60	                return []
61	
62	    def _save(self, path: Path, records: list[dict]) -> None:
63	        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
64	            json.dump(records, fh, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
65	
66	    # --- predictions ---
67	
68	    def insert_prediction(self, pred: Prediction) -> None:
69	        records = self._load(self._predictions_file)
70	        records.append(pred.to_dict())
71	        self._save(self._predictions_file, records)
72	
73	    def update_prediction(self, pred: Prediction) -> None:
74	        records = self._load(self._predictions_file)
75	        for i, r in enumerate(records):
76	            if r["id"] == pred.id:
77	                records[i] = pred.to_dict()
78	                break
79	        self._save(self._predictions_file, records)
80	
81	    def get_prediction(self, pred_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:
82	        for r in self._load(self._predictions_file):
83	            if r["id"] == pred_id:
84	                return r
85	        return None
86	
87	    def list_predictions(self) -> list[dict]:
88	        return self._load(self._predictions_file)
89	
90	    # --- decisions ---
91	
92	    def insert_decision(self, dec: Decision) -> None:
93	        records = self._load(self._decisions_file)
94	        records.append(dec.to_dict())
95	        self._save(self._decisions_file, records)
96	
97	    def update_decision(self, dec: Decision) -> None:
98	        records = self._load(self._decisions_file)
99	        for i, r in enumerate(records):
100	            if r["id"] == dec.id:
101	                records[i] = dec.to_dict()
102	                break
103	        self._save(self._decisions_file, records)
104	
105	    def get_decision(self, dec_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:
106	        for r in self._load(self._decisions_file):
107	            if r["id"] == dec_id:
108	                return r
109	        return None
110	
111	    def list_decisions(self) -> list[dict]:
112	        return self._load(self._decisions_file)
113	
114	
115	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
116	# OutcomeTracker (public API)
117	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
118	
119	_DEFAULT_DATA_DIR = (
120	    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]  # repo root: master_investments/
121	    / "data"
122	    / "intelligence"
123	)
124	
125	# Reminder thresholds: warn when prediction is older than these without resolution
126	_REMINDER_DAYS = [7, 30, 90]
127	
128	
129	class OutcomeTracker:
130	    """
131	    Log and query predictions/decisions made by the intelligence system.
132	
133	    Parameters
134	    ----------
135	    data_dir:
136	        Directory for JSON fallback storage. Defaults to
137	        ``<repo>/data/intelligence/``.
138	
139	    Example
140	    -------
141	    >>> tracker = OutcomeTracker()
142	    >>> pid = tracker.log_prediction(
143	    ...     prediction="BTC breaks $100K within 90 days",
144	    ...     confidence=0.65,
145	    ...     timeframe="90d",
146	    ...     signals=["hash-rate-ath", "etf-inflow-spike"],
147	    ...     reasoning="Hash rate at ATH + institutional inflows accelerating",
148	    ... )
149	    >>> tracker.get_prediction(pid)
150	    """
151	
152	    def __init__(self, data_dir: Optional[Path] = None) -> None:
153	        self._data_dir = Path(data_dir) if data_dir else _DEFAULT_DATA_DIR
154	        self._store = _JsonFallbackStore(self._data_dir)
155	        if _DB_AVAILABLE:
156	            logger.info("timeseries.py available — will use DB backend when wired")
157	        else:
158	            logger.debug("timeseries.py not yet available — using JSON fallback store")
159	
160	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
161	    # Prediction logging
162	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
163	
164	    def log_prediction(
165	        self,
166	        prediction: str,
167	        confidence: float,
168	        timeframe: str,
169	        signals: list[str],
170	        reasoning: str,
171	    ) -> str:
172	        """
173	        Record a new forward-looking prediction.
174	
175	        Parameters
176	        ----------
177	        prediction:
178	            Plain-text statement of what is predicted.
179	        confidence:
180	            Probability 0.0–1.0 at time of logging.
181	        timeframe:
182	            Resolution window, e.g. ``"30d"``, ``"90d"``, ``"6mo"``.
183	        signals:
184	            List of signal IDs or descriptors used to derive the prediction.
185	        reasoning:
186	            Narrative explaining how signals lead to the prediction.
187	
188	        Returns
189	        -------
190	        str
191	            Prediction ID (``PRED-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<hex6>``).
192	        """
193	        if not prediction.strip():
194	            raise ValueError("prediction text must not be empty")
195	        if not 0.0 <= confidence <= 1.0:
196	            raise ValueError(f"confidence must be 0.0–1.0, got {confidence}")
197	        if not timeframe.strip():
198	            raise ValueError("timeframe must not be empty")
199	
200	        pred_id = f"PRED-{datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}-{uuid4().hex[:6]}"
201	        pred = Prediction(
202	            id=pred_id,
203	            made_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
204	            prediction=prediction.strip(),
205	            confidence=confidence,
206	            timeframe=timeframe.strip(),
207	            signals_used=list(signals),
208	            reasoning=reasoning.strip(),
209	        )
210	        self._store.insert_prediction(pred)
211	        logger.info("Logged prediction %s (confidence=%.2f, timeframe=%s)", pred_id, confidence, timeframe)
212	        return pred_id
213	
214	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
215	    # Decision logging
216	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
217	
218	    def log_decision(
219	        self,
220	        decision: str,
221	        alternatives: list[str],
222	        expected_outcome: str,
223	    ) -> str:
224	        """
225	        Record an operator decision for accountability and later review.
226	
227	        Parameters
228	        ----------
229	        decision:
230	            Plain-text description of the action taken.
231	        alternatives:
232	            Other options that were considered but not chosen.
233	        expected_outcome:
234	            What the decision-maker expects to happen as a result.

"""
Outcome Tracker - Log predictions and decisions to SQLite via db/timeseries.py.

Designed to extend the existing /log-outcome skill with intelligence-layer
tracking (market predictions, opportunity bets, operator decisions).

Storage contract
----------------
Depends on `.claude/lib/intelligence/db/timeseries.py` (Phase 0A).
If that module is not yet available, falls back to local JSON files so this
module is independently usable during parallel development.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional
from uuid import uuid4

from .schemas import Decision, OutcomeCode, Prediction

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Storage backend abstraction (thin wrapper — swapped when timeseries is ready)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_DB_AVAILABLE = False

try:
    # Phase 0A delivers this module; import lazily so we don't hard-block
    from ..db.timeseries import TimeseriesDB  # type: ignore[import]
    _DB_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    TimeseriesDB = None  # type: ignore[assignment,misc]


class _JsonFallbackStore:
    """
    Minimal append-only JSON store used when timeseries.py is unavailable.
    Two files: predictions.json + decisions.json under data_dir.
    """

    def __init__(self, data_dir: Path) -> None:
        data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._predictions_file = data_dir / "predictions.json"
        self._decisions_file = data_dir / "decisions.json"

    def _load(self, path: Path) -> list[dict]:
        if not path.exists():
            return []
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            try:
                return json.load(fh)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                logger.warning("Corrupt JSON at %s — starting fresh", path)
                return []

    def _save(self, path: Path, records: list[dict]) -> None:
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(records, fh, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

    # --- predictions ---

    def insert_prediction(self, pred: Prediction) -> None:
        records = self._load(self._predictions_file)
        records.append(pred.to_dict())
        self._save(self._predictions_file, records)

    def update_prediction(self, pred: Prediction) -> None:
        records = self._load(self._predictions_file)
        for i, r in enumerate(records):
            if r["id"] == pred.id:
                records[i] = pred.to_dict()
                break
        self._save(self._predictions_file, records)

    def get_prediction(self, pred_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:
        for r in self._load(self._predictions_file):
            if r["id"] == pred_id:
                return r
        return None

    def list_predictions(self) -> list[dict]:
        return self._load(self._predictions_file)

    # --- decisions ---

    def insert_decision(self, dec: Decision) -> None:
        records = self._load(self._decisions_file)
        records.append(dec.to_dict())
        self._save(self._decisions_file, records)

    def update_decision(self, dec: Decision) -> None:
        records = self._load(self._decisions_file)
        for i, r in enumerate(records):
            if r["id"] == dec.id:
                records[i] = dec.to_dict()
                break
        self._save(self._decisions_file, records)

    def get_decision(self, dec_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:
        for r in self._load(self._decisions_file):
            if r["id"] == dec_id:
                return r
        return None

    def list_decisions(self) -> list[dict]:
        return self._load(self._decisions_file)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OutcomeTracker (public API)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_DEFAULT_DATA_DIR = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]  # repo root: master_investments/
    / "data"
    / "intelligence"
)

# Reminder thresholds: warn when prediction is older than these without resolution
_REMINDER_DAYS = [7, 30, 90]


class OutcomeTracker:
    """
    Log and query predictions/decisions made by the intelligence system.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data_dir:
        Directory for JSON fallback storage. Defaults to
        ``<repo>/data/intelligence/``.

    Example
    -------
    >>> tracker = OutcomeTracker()
    >>> pid = tracker.log_prediction(
    ...     prediction="BTC breaks $100K within 90 days",
    ...     confidence=0.65,
    ...     timeframe="90d",
    ...     signals=["hash-rate-ath", "etf-inflow-spike"],
    ...     reasoning="Hash rate at ATH + institutional inflows accelerating",
    ... )
    >>> tracker.get_prediction(pid)
    """

    def __init__(self, data_dir: Optional[Path] = None) -> None:
        self._data_dir = Path(data_dir) if data_dir else _DEFAULT_DATA_DIR
        self._store = _JsonFallbackStore(self._data_dir)
        if _DB_AVAILABLE:
            logger.info("timeseries.py available — will use DB backend when wired")
        else:
            logger.debug("timeseries.py not yet available — using JSON fallback store")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Prediction logging
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def log_prediction(
        self,
        prediction: str,
        confidence: float,
        timeframe: str,
        signals: list[str],
        reasoning: str,
    ) -> str:
        """
        Record a new forward-looking prediction.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prediction:
            Plain-text statement of what is predicted.
        confidence:
            Probability 0.0–1.0 at time of logging.
        timeframe:
            Resolution window, e.g. ``"30d"``, ``"90d"``, ``"6mo"``.
        signals:
            List of signal IDs or descriptors used to derive the prediction.
        reasoning:
            Narrative explaining how signals lead to the prediction.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            Prediction ID (``PRED-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<hex6>``).
        """
        if not prediction.strip():
            raise ValueError("prediction text must not be empty")
        if not 0.0 <= confidence <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError(f"confidence must be 0.0–1.0, got {confidence}")
        if not timeframe.strip():
            raise ValueError("timeframe must not be empty")

        pred_id = f"PRED-{datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}-{uuid4().hex[:6]}"
        pred = Prediction(
            id=pred_id,
            made_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
            prediction=prediction.strip(),
            confidence=confidence,
            timeframe=timeframe.strip(),
            signals_used=list(signals),
            reasoning=reasoning.strip(),
        )
        self._store.insert_prediction(pred)
        logger.info("Logged prediction %s (confidence=%.2f, timeframe=%s)", pred_id, confidence, timeframe)
        return pred_id

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Decision logging
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def log_decision(
        self,
        decision: str,
        alternatives: list[str],
        expected_outcome: str,
    ) -> str:
        """
        Record an operator decision for accountability and later review.

        Parameters
        ----------
        decision:
            Plain-text description of the action taken.
        alternatives:
            Other options that were considered but not chosen.
        expected_outcome:
            What the decision-maker expects to happen as a result.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            Decision ID (``DEC-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<hex6>``).
        """
        if not decision.strip():
            raise ValueError("decision text must not be empty")

        dec_id = f"DEC-{datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}-{uuid4().hex[:6]}"
        dec = Decision(
            id=dec_id,
            made_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
            decision=decision.strip(),
            alternatives=list(alternatives),
            expected_outcome=expected_outcome.strip(),
        )
        self._store.insert_decision(dec)
        logger.info("Logged decision %s", dec_id)
        return dec_id

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Queries
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def get_prediction(self, pred_id: str) -> Optional[Prediction]:
        """
        Retrieve a prediction by ID.

        Returns ``None`` if not found.
        """
        raw = self._store.get_prediction(pred_id)
        if raw is None:
            return None
        return Prediction.from_dict(raw)

    def get_decision(self, dec_id: str) -> Optional[Decision]:
        """
        Retrieve a decision by ID.

        Returns ``None`` if not found.
        """
        raw = self._store.get_decision(dec_id)
        if raw is None:
            return None
        return Decision.from_dict(raw)

    def get_unresolved_predictions(self, older_than_days: int = 0) -> list[Prediction]:
        """
        Return all predictions that have not yet been resolved.

        Parameters
        ----------
        older_than_days:
            When > 0, only return predictions whose ``made_at`` is older than
            this many days. Use this to surface stale predictions that need
            attention (e.g. ``older_than_days=30``).

        Returns
        -------
        list[Prediction]
            Sorted oldest-first.
        """
        cutoff = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=older_than_days) if older_than_days > 0 else None

        unresolved: list[Prediction] = []
        for raw in self._store.list_predictions():
            pred = Prediction.from_dict(raw)
            if pred.is_resolved:
                continue
            if cutoff is not None and pred.made_at > cutoff:
                continue  # too recent — skip
            unresolved.append(pred)

        return sorted(unresolved, key=lambda p: p.made_at)

    def get_due_reminders(self) -> list[tuple[Prediction, int]]:
        """
        Return predictions that have crossed a reminder threshold
        (7, 30, or 90 days old) without resolution.

        Returns
        -------
        list[tuple[Prediction, int]]
            Each element is ``(prediction, days_threshold_crossed)``.
        """
        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        due: list[tuple[Prediction, int]] = []

        for raw in self._store.list_predictions():
            pred = Prediction.from_dict(raw)
            if pred.is_resolved:
                continue
            age_days = (now - pred.made_at).days
            for threshold in sorted(_REMINDER_DAYS, reverse=True):
                if age_days >= threshold:
                    due.append((pred, threshold))
                    break  # only emit highest crossed threshold per prediction

        return due

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Internal helpers (used by resolver.py)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _update_prediction(self, pred: Prediction) -> None:
        """Persist an updated Prediction (called by resolver)."""
        self._store.update_prediction(pred)

    def _update_decision(self, dec: Decision) -> None:
        """Persist an updated Decision (called by resolver)."""
        self._store.update_decision(dec)

"""
Outcome Tracker Schemas - Prediction and Decision data models.

Covers intelligence-layer predictions (market calls, opportunity bets) and
operator decisions (invest, pivot, exit). Distinct from the cash-flow
experience_layer schemas which track advisor recommendations.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum
from typing import Optional
import json


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outcome codes (S / P / F / N)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class OutcomeCode(str, Enum):
    """S=Success, P=Partial, F=Failure, N=Not applicable."""
    SUCCESS = "S"
    PARTIAL = "P"
    FAILURE = "F"
    NOT_APPLICABLE = "N"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prediction schema
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class Prediction:
    """
    A forward-looking prediction made by the intelligence system.

    Fields
    ------
    id              : Unique identifier — format ``PRED-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<hex6>``
    made_at         : When the prediction was created (UTC)
    prediction      : Plain-text statement of what is predicted
    confidence      : 0.0–1.0 probability estimate at time of prediction
    timeframe       : Human-readable window, e.g. "30d", "90d", "6mo"
    signals_used    : List of signal IDs or descriptors that drove the call
    reasoning       : Explanation of how signals led to the prediction
    resolved_at     : When actual outcome was recorded (None if still open)
    actual_outcome  : Plain-text description of what actually happened
    accuracy_score  : 0.0–1.0 post-hoc accuracy; None until resolved
    """

    id: str
    made_at: datetime
    prediction: str
    confidence: float  # 0.0–1.0
    timeframe: str     # e.g. "30d", "90d", "6mo"
    signals_used: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    reasoning: str = ""
    resolved_at: Optional[datetime] = None
    actual_outcome: Optional[str] = None
    accuracy_score: Optional[float] = None  # None until resolved

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not 0.0 <= self.confidence <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError(f"confidence must be 0.0–1.0, got {self.confidence}")
        if self.accuracy_score is not None and not 0.0 <= self.accuracy_score <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError(f"accuracy_score must be 0.0–1.0, got {self.accuracy_score}")

    @property
    def is_resolved(self) -> bool:
        return self.resolved_at is not None

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        d = asdict(self)
        # Convert datetimes to ISO strings for JSON serialization
        d["made_at"] = self.made_at.isoformat()
        d["resolved_at"] = self.resolved_at.isoformat() if self.resolved_at else None
        return d

    def to_json(self, indent: int = 2) -> str:
        return json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=indent)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> "Prediction":
        return cls(
            id=data["id"],
            made_at=datetime.fromisoformat(data["made_at"]),
            prediction=data["prediction"],
            confidence=float(data["confidence"]),
            timeframe=data["timeframe"],
            signals_used=data.get("signals_used", []),
            reasoning=data.get("reasoning", ""),
            resolved_at=datetime.fromisoformat(data["resolved_at"]) if data.get("resolved_at") else None,
            actual_outcome=data.get("actual_outcome"),
            accuracy_score=float(data["accuracy_score"]) if data.get("accuracy_score") is not None else None,
        )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision schema
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class Decision:
    """
    An operator decision logged for accountability and learning.

    Fields
    ------
    id              : Unique identifier — format ``DEC-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<hex6>``
    made_at         : When the decision was made (UTC)
    decision        : Plain-text description of the action taken
    alternatives    : Other options that were considered but not chosen
    expected_outcome: What the decision-maker predicted would happen
    result          : Actual result observed (None until resolved)
    variance        : Narrative delta between expected and actual (None until resolved)
    """

    id: str
    made_at: datetime
    decision: str
    alternatives: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    expected_outcome: str = ""
    result: Optional[str] = None
    variance: Optional[str] = None  # None until resolved

    @property
    def is_resolved(self) -> bool:
        return self.result is not None

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        d = asdict(self)
        d["made_at"] = self.made_at.isoformat()
        return d

    def to_json(self, indent: int = 2) -> str:
        return json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=indent)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> "Decision":

1	"""Fitness Scorer — Brier-based composite scoring and evaluation for mutations."""
2	
3	from statistics import mean
4	from typing import Optional
5	
6	from .registry import EvolutionRegistry
7	from .schemas import EvalResult
8	
9	BRIER_WEIGHT = 0.6
10	YIELD_WEIGHT = 0.25
11	PARSE_WEIGHT = 0.15
12	MIN_CASES = 5
13	PROMOTION_THRESHOLD = 1.15
14	ROLLBACK_THRESHOLD = 0.20
15	ROLLBACK_WINDOW = 3
16	
17	
18	class FitnessScorer:
19	    def __init__(self, registry: EvolutionRegistry):
20	        self.registry = registry
21	
22	    def compute_fitness(self, variant_id: int) -> Optional[float]:
23	        """Compute composite fitness from all fitness_log entries for this variant."""
24	        entries = self.registry.get_fitness_entries(variant_id)
25	        if not entries:
26	            return None
27	
28	        brier_scores = [e.brier_score for e in entries if e.brier_score is not None]
29	        yields = [e.fact_yield for e in entries]
30	        parses = [e.parse_success for e in entries]
31	
32	        if not yields:
33	            return None
34	
35	        brier_component = (1.0 - mean(brier_scores)) if brier_scores else 0.5
36	        yield_component = min(mean(yields) / 3.0, 1.0)  # normalize: 3 facts = max
37	        parse_component = mean(parses)
38	
39	        return (
40	            brier_component * BRIER_WEIGHT
41	            + yield_component * YIELD_WEIGHT
42	            + parse_component * PARSE_WEIGHT
43	        )
44	
45	    def evaluate(self, mutation_id: int) -> EvalResult:
46	        """Evaluate mutation: PENDING, PROMOTE, or KILL."""
47	        variants = self.registry.get_variants(mutation_id)
48	        if not variants:
49	            return EvalResult(decision="KILL", reason="no variants")
50	
51	        original = next((v for v in variants if v.variant_index == 0), None)
52	        if not original:
53	            return EvalResult(decision="KILL", reason="no original variant")
54	
55	        if original.cases_tested < MIN_CASES:
56	            return EvalResult(
57	                decision="PENDING",
58	                reason=f"insufficient cases ({original.cases_tested}/{MIN_CASES})",
59	            )
60	
61	        scores: dict[int, float] = {}
62	        for v in variants:
63	            score = self.compute_fitness(v.id)
64	            if score is not None:
65	                scores[v.id] = score
66	
67	        original_score = scores.get(original.id)
68	        if original_score is None or original_score == 0.0:
69	            return EvalResult(decision="PENDING", reason="original not scored yet")
70	
71	        best_id = None
72	        best_score = 0.0
73	        for vid, score in scores.items():
74	            if vid != original.id and score > best_score:
75	                best_id = vid
76	                best_score = score
77	
78	        if best_id and best_score >= original_score * PROMOTION_THRESHOLD:
79	            improvement = (best_score - original_score) / original_score
80	            return EvalResult(
81	                decision="PROMOTE",
82	                winner_id=best_id,
83	                improvement_pct=round(improvement, 4),
84	                reason=f"variant beats original by {improvement:.1%}",
85	            )
86	
87	        return EvalResult(
88	            decision="KILL",
89	            reason=f"best={best_score:.3f} < threshold={original_score * PROMOTION_THRESHOLD:.3f}",
90	        )
91	
92	    def check_regression(self, mutation_id: int) -> bool:
93	        """Post-promotion regression check. Returns True if rollback needed."""
94	        variants = self.registry.get_variants(mutation_id)
95	        winner = next((v for v in variants if v.is_winner), None)
96	        original = next((v for v in variants if v.variant_index == 0), None)
97	
98	        if not winner or not original:
99	            return False
100	
101	        winner_entries = self.registry.get_fitness_entries(winner.id)
102	        if len(winner_entries) < ROLLBACK_WINDOW:
103	            return False
104	
105	        recent = winner_entries[-ROLLBACK_WINDOW:]
106	        recent_yields = [e.fact_yield for e in recent]
107	        recent_parses = [e.parse_success for e in recent]
108	
109	        all_entries = self.registry.get_fitness_entries(winner.id)
110	        pre_promo = all_entries[:-ROLLBACK_WINDOW] if len(all_entries) > ROLLBACK_WINDOW else []
111	
112	        if not pre_promo:
113	            return False
114	
115	        pre_yield = mean([e.fact_yield for e in pre_promo])
116	        post_yield = mean(recent_yields)
117	
118	        if pre_yield > 0 and (pre_yield - post_yield) / pre_yield > ROLLBACK_THRESHOLD:
119	            return True
120	
121	        pre_parse = mean([e.parse_success for e in pre_promo])
122	        post_parse = mean(recent_parses)
123	
124	        if pre_parse > 0 and (pre_parse - post_parse) / pre_parse > ROLLBACK_THRESHOLD:
125	            return True
126	
127	        return False

1	"""Evolution Registry — SQLite persistence for mutations, variants, and fitness tracking."""
2	
3	import sqlite3
4	from datetime import datetime, timezone
5	from pathlib import Path
6	from typing import Optional
7	
8	from .schemas import Mutation, Variant, FitnessEntry
9	
10	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
11	DEFAULT_DB = ROOT / "data" / "evolution" / "evolution-registry.db"
12	
13	SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
14	
15	
16	class EvolutionRegistry:
17	    def __init__(self, db_path: Optional[Path] = None):
18	        self.db_path = db_path or DEFAULT_DB
19	        self.db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
20	        self._ensure_tables()
21	
22	    def _conn(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
23	        conn = sqlite3.connect(str(self.db_path))
24	        conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
25	        conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
26	        return conn
27	
28	    def _ensure_tables(self):
29	        with self._conn() as conn:
30	            conn.executescript("""
31	                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_meta (
32	                    key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
33	                    value TEXT NOT NULL
34	                );
35	
36	                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mutations (
37	                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
38	                    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
39	                    component TEXT NOT NULL,
40	                    target_path TEXT NOT NULL,
41	                    parent_id INTEGER REFERENCES mutations(id),
42	                    variant_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
43	                    status TEXT DEFAULT 'testing',
44	                    fitness_before REAL,
45	                    fitness_after REAL,
46	                    improvement_pct REAL,
47	                    promoted_at TEXT,
48	                    killed_at TEXT
49	                );
50	
51	                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS variants (
52	                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
53	                    mutation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES mutations(id),
54	                    variant_index INTEGER NOT NULL,
55	                    content TEXT NOT NULL,
56	                    fitness_score REAL,
57	                    cases_tested INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
58	                    is_winner INTEGER DEFAULT 0
59	                );
60	
61	                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fitness_log (
62	                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
63	                    variant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES variants(id),
64	                    case_id TEXT NOT NULL,
65	                    brier_score REAL,
66	                    fact_yield REAL NOT NULL,
67	                    parse_success REAL NOT NULL,
68	                    timestamp TEXT NOT NULL
69	                );
70	
71	                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_mutations_component
72	                    ON mutations(component);
73	                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_mutations_status
74	                    ON mutations(status);
75	                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_variants_mutation
76	                    ON variants(mutation_id);
77	                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fitness_variant
78	                    ON fitness_log(variant_id);
79	                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fitness_case
80	                    ON fitness_log(case_id);
81	            """)
82	            conn.execute(
83	                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO schema_meta (key, value) VALUES (?, ?)",
84	                ("version", str(SCHEMA_VERSION))
85	            )
86	
87	    def _now(self) -> str:
88	        return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
89	
90	    # --- Mutations ---
91	
92	    def create_mutation(
93	        self, component: str, target_path: str, parent_id: Optional[int] = None
94	    ) -> Mutation:
95	        now = self._now()
96	        with self._conn() as conn:
97	            cursor = conn.execute(
98	                "INSERT INTO mutations (created_at, component, target_path, parent_id, status) "
99	                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'testing')",
100	                (now, component, target_path, parent_id),
101	            )
102	            mid = cursor.lastrowid
103	        return Mutation(
104	            id=mid, created_at=now, component=component,
105	            target_path=target_path, parent_id=parent_id,
106	            variant_count=0, status="testing",
107	            fitness_before=None, fitness_after=None, improvement_pct=None,
108	        )
109	
110	    def get_mutation(self, mutation_id: int) -> Optional[Mutation]:
111	        with self._conn() as conn:
112	            row = conn.execute(
113	                "SELECT * FROM mutations WHERE id=?", (mutation_id,)
114	            ).fetchone()
115	        if not row:
116	            return None
117	        return self._row_to_mutation(row)
118	
119	    def get_active_mutations(self, component: Optional[str] = None) -> list[Mutation]:
120	        with self._conn() as conn:
121	            if component:
122	                rows = conn.execute(
123	                    "SELECT * FROM mutations WHERE status='testing' AND component=?",
124	                    (component,),
125	                ).fetchall()
126	            else:
127	                rows = conn.execute(
128	                    "SELECT * FROM mutations WHERE status='testing'"
129	                ).fetchall()
130	        return [self._row_to_mutation(r) for r in rows]
131	
132	    def get_recently_promoted(self, days: int = 30) -> list[Mutation]:
133	        from datetime import timedelta
134	        cutoff = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=days)).isoformat()
135	        with self._conn() as conn:
136	            rows = conn.execute(
137	                "SELECT * FROM mutations WHERE status='promoted' AND promoted_at >= ? "
138	                "ORDER BY promoted_at DESC LIMIT 20",
139	                (cutoff,),
140	            ).fetchall()
141	        return [self._row_to_mutation(r) for r in rows]
142	
143	    def get_lineage(self, mutation_id: int, depth: int = 10) -> list[Mutation]:
144	        chain = []
145	        current_id = mutation_id
146	        for _ in range(depth):
147	            m = self.get_mutation(current_id)
148	            if not m:
149	                break
150	            chain.append(m)
151	            if not m.parent_id:
152	                break
153	            current_id = m.parent_id
154	        return chain
155	
156	    # --- Variants ---
157	
158	    def add_variant(self, mutation_id: int, index: int, content: str) -> Variant:
159	        with self._conn() as conn:
160	            cursor = conn.execute(
161	                "INSERT INTO variants (mutation_id, variant_index, content) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
162	                (mutation_id, index, content),
163	            )
164	            vid = cursor.lastrowid
165	            conn.execute(
166	                "UPDATE mutations SET variant_count = variant_count + 1 WHERE id=?",
167	                (mutation_id,),
168	            )
169	        return Variant(
170	            id=vid, mutation_id=mutation_id, variant_index=index,
171	            content=content, fitness_score=None, cases_tested=0, is_winner=False,
172	        )
173	
174	    def get_variants(self, mutation_id: int) -> list[Variant]:
175	        with self._conn() as conn:
176	            rows = conn.execute(
177	                "SELECT * FROM variants WHERE mutation_id=? ORDER BY variant_index",
178	                (mutation_id,),
179	            ).fetchall()
180	        return [self._row_to_variant(r) for r in rows]
181	
182	    def get_variant(self, variant_id: int) -> Optional[Variant]:
183	        with self._conn() as conn:
184	            row = conn.execute(
185	                "SELECT * FROM variants WHERE id=?", (variant_id,)
186	            ).fetchone()
187	        if not row:
188	            return None
189	        return self._row_to_variant(row)
190	
191	    def get_variant_by_index(self, mutation_id: int, index: int) -> Optional[Variant]:
192	        with self._conn() as conn:
193	            row = conn.execute(
194	                "SELECT * FROM variants WHERE mutation_id=? AND variant_index=?",
195	                (mutation_id, index),
196	            ).fetchone()
197	        if not row:
198	            return None
199	        return self._row_to_variant(row)
200	
201	    # --- Fitness ---
202	
203	    def log_fitness(
204	        self, variant_id: int, case_id: str,
205	        brier: Optional[float], fact_yield: float, parse_success: float
206	    ) -> FitnessEntry:
207	        now = self._now()
208	        with self._conn() as conn:
209	            cursor = conn.execute(
210	                "INSERT INTO fitness_log (variant_id, case_id, brier_score, fact_yield, parse_success, timestamp) "
211	                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
212	                (variant_id, case_id, brier, fact_yield, parse_success, now),
213	            )
214	            fid = cursor.lastrowid
215	            conn.execute(
216	                "UPDATE variants SET cases_tested = cases_tested + 1 WHERE id=?",
217	                (variant_id,),
218	            )
219	        return FitnessEntry(
220	            id=fid, variant_id=variant_id, case_id=case_id,
221	            brier_score=brier, fact_yield=fact_yield,
222	            parse_success=parse_success, timestamp=now,
223	        )
224	
225	    def get_fitness_entries(self, variant_id: int) -> list[FitnessEntry]:
226	        with self._conn() as conn:
227	            rows = conn.execute(
228	                "SELECT * FROM fitness_log WHERE variant_id=? ORDER BY timestamp",
229	                (variant_id,),
230	            ).fetchall()
231	        return [self._row_to_fitness(r) for r in rows]
232	
233	    def update_brier_for_case(self, case_id: str, brier_score: float):
234	        with self._conn() as conn:
235	            conn.execute(
236	                "UPDATE fitness_log SET brier_score=? WHERE case_id=? AND brier_score IS NULL",
237	                (brier_score, case_id),
238	            )
239	
240	    # --- Status transitions ---
241	
242	    def promote_variant(self, variant_id: int):
243	        now = self._now()
244	        with self._conn() as conn:
245	            row = conn.execute(
246	                "SELECT mutation_id, fitness_score FROM variants WHERE id=?", (variant_id,)
247	            ).fetchone()
248	            if not row:
249	                return
250	            mutation_id, fitness = row
251	            conn.execute(
252	                "UPDATE variants SET is_winner=1 WHERE id=?", (variant_id,)
253	            )
254	            conn.execute(
255	                "UPDATE mutations SET status='promoted', promoted_at=?, fitness_after=? WHERE id=?",
256	                (now, fitness, mutation_id),
257	            )
258	
259	    def kill_mutation(self, mutation_id: int):
260	        now = self._now()
261	        with self._conn() as conn:
262	            conn.execute(
263	                "UPDATE mutations SET status='killed', killed_at=? WHERE id=?",
264	                (now, mutation_id),
265	            )
266	
267	    def rollback_mutation(self, mutation_id: int):
268	        now = self._now()
269	        with self._conn() as conn:
270	            conn.execute(
271	                "UPDATE mutations SET status='rolled_back', killed_at=? WHERE id=?",
272	                (now, mutation_id),
273	            )
274	            conn.execute(
275	                "UPDATE variants SET is_winner=0 WHERE mutation_id=?", (mutation_id,)
276	            )
277	
278	    # --- Row mappers ---
279	
280	    def _row_to_mutation(self, row: tuple) -> Mutation:
281	        return Mutation(
282	            id=row[0], created_at=row[1], component=row[2],
283	            target_path=row[3], parent_id=row[4], variant_count=row[5],
284	            status=row[6], fitness_before=row[7], fitness_after=row[8],
285	            improvement_pct=row[9], promoted_at=row[10], killed_at=row[11],
286	        )
287	
288	    def _row_to_variant(self, row: tuple) -> Variant:
289	        return Variant(
290	            id=row[0], mutation_id=row[1], variant_index=row[2],
291	            content=row[3], fitness_score=row[4], cases_tested=row[5],
292	            is_winner=bool(row[6]),
293	        )
294	
295	    def _row_to_fitness(self, row: tuple) -> FitnessEntry:
296	        return FitnessEntry(
297	            id=row[0], variant_id=row[1], case_id=row[2],
298	            brier_score=row[3], fact_yield=row[4], parse_success=row[5],
299	            timestamp=row[6],
300	        )

1	"""
2	fitness.py — Multi-metric fitness scoring for strategy evaluation.
3	
4	Fitness = 0.5*brier_improvement + 0.2*correct_ratio + 0.2*info_gain + 0.1*diversity_bonus
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import json
10	import logging
11	from dataclasses import dataclass
12	from pathlib import Path
13	from typing import Optional
14	
15	from .schema import Strategy
16	
17	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
18	
19	_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5]
20	_BRIER_PATH = _REPO_ROOT / "data" / "calibration" / "brier-scores.jsonl"
21	
22	
23	@dataclass
24	class FitnessScore:
25	    strategy_id: str
26	    brier_improvement_rate: float
27	    correct_verdict_ratio: float
28	    information_gain: float
29	    diversity_bonus: float
30	    total: float
31	    verdicts_evaluated: int
32	    window_start: int
33	    window_end: int
34	
35	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
36	        return {
37	            "strategy_id": self.strategy_id,
38	            "brier_improvement_rate": round(self.brier_improvement_rate, 4),
39	            "correct_verdict_ratio": round(self.correct_verdict_ratio, 4),
40	            "information_gain": round(self.information_gain, 4),
41	            "diversity_bonus": round(self.diversity_bonus, 4),
42	            "total": round(self.total, 4),
43	            "verdicts_evaluated": self.verdicts_evaluated,
44	            "window": [self.window_start, self.window_end],
45	        }
46	
47	
48	class StrategyFitness:
49	    WEIGHTS = {
50	        "brier_improvement_rate": 0.50,
51	        "correct_verdict_ratio": 0.20,
52	        "information_gain": 0.20,
53	        "diversity_bonus": 0.10,
54	    }
55	
56	    def __init__(self, sandbox_results_path: Optional[Path] = None):
57	        self._sandbox_path = sandbox_results_path or (
58	            _REPO_ROOT / "data" / "evolution" / "sandbox-results.jsonl"
59	        )
60	
61	    def score(
62	        self,
63	        strategy: Strategy,
64	        population: list[Strategy],
65	        window_size: int = 10,
66	    ) -> FitnessScore:
67	        """Compute fitness for a strategy over recent window."""
68	        sandbox_results = self._get_strategy_results(strategy.id)
69	        evaluated = [r for r in sandbox_results if r.get("actual_outcome")]
70	
71	        n = min(window_size, len(evaluated))
72	        window = evaluated[-n:] if n > 0 else []
73	
74	        brier_rate = self._brier_improvement_rate(strategy)
75	        correct_ratio = self._correct_verdict_ratio(strategy.id, window)
76	        info_gain = self._information_gain(strategy, window)
77	        diversity = self._diversity_bonus(strategy, population)
78	
79	        total = (
80	            self.WEIGHTS["brier_improvement_rate"] * brier_rate
81	            + self.WEIGHTS["correct_verdict_ratio"] * correct_ratio
82	            + self.WEIGHTS["information_gain"] * info_gain
83	            + self.WEIGHTS["diversity_bonus"] * diversity
84	        )
85	
86	        return FitnessScore(
87	            strategy_id=strategy.id,
88	            brier_improvement_rate=brier_rate,
89	            correct_verdict_ratio=correct_ratio,
90	            information_gain=info_gain,
91	            diversity_bonus=diversity,
92	            total=total,
93	            verdicts_evaluated=n,
94	            window_start=strategy.total_verdicts - n,
95	            window_end=strategy.total_verdicts,
96	        )
97	
98	    def _brier_improvement_rate(self, strategy: Strategy) -> float:
99	        """Rate of Brier score improvement across fitness history."""
100	        history = strategy.fitness_history
101	        if len(history) < 2:
102	            return 0.5
103	
104	        briers = [h.get("avg_brier", 0.5) for h in history if "avg_brier" in h]
105	        if len(briers) < 2:
106	            return 0.5
107	
108	        improvements = 0
109	        for i in range(1, len(briers)):
110	            if briers[i] < briers[i - 1]:
111	                improvements += 1
112	
113	        return improvements / (len(briers) - 1)
114	
115	    def _correct_verdict_ratio(self, strategy_id: str, window: list[dict]) -> float:
116	        """Fraction of verdicts where strategy was correct."""
117	        if not window:
118	            return 0.5
119	
120	        correct = 0
121	        for r in window:
122	            cf = r.get("counterfactuals", {}).get(strategy_id, {})
123	            verdict = cf.get("verdict", "")
124	            outcome = r.get("actual_outcome", "")
125	            if self._matches(verdict, outcome):
126	                correct += 1
127	
128	        return correct / len(window)
129	
130	    def _information_gain(self, strategy: Strategy, window: list[dict]) -> float:
131	        """How much new signal compared to parent strategy."""
132	        if not strategy.parent_id or not window:
133	            return 0.5
134	
135	        parent_correct = 0
136	        child_correct = 0
137	        for r in window:
138	            cfs = r.get("counterfactuals", {})
139	            parent_cf = cfs.get(strategy.parent_id, {})
140	            child_cf = cfs.get(strategy.id, {})
141	            outcome = r.get("actual_outcome", "")
142	
143	            if self._matches(parent_cf.get("verdict", ""), outcome):
144	                parent_correct += 1
145	            if self._matches(child_cf.get("verdict", ""), outcome):
146	                child_correct += 1
147	
148	        if not window:
149	            return 0.5
150	        parent_rate = parent_correct / len(window)

180	    def check_regression_and_revert(self, recent_scores: list[float]) -> bool:
181	        """Auto-revert if last meta-meta made things worse."""
182	        history = self._load_history()
183	        if not history:
184	            return False
185	
186	        last = history[-1]
187	        if not last.get("mutation_applied"):
188	            return False
189	
190	        if len(recent_scores) < 2:
191	            return False
192	
193	        if all(s < recent_scores[0] for s in recent_scores[1:]):
194	            config = self._load_config()
195	            param = last["mutation_applied"]
196	            old_val = last.get("old_value")
197	            if old_val is not None and param in config:
198	                config[param] = old_val
199	                self._save_config(config)

206	        if not history:
207	            return True
208	        last_ts = history[-1].get("timestamp", "")
209	        if not last_ts:
210	            return True
211	        try:
212	            last_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(last_ts)
213	            return (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - last_dt) > timedelta(days=MIN_INTERVAL_DAYS)
214	        except (ValueError, TypeError):

222	            new = min(1.0, old + MAX_PARAM_ADJUSTMENT)

227	            old = config.get(param, 3)
